input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 is a reverse MFN/right-of-first-refusal running against Customer: it is open-ended (any more favourable commercial offer, any other provider, no product limit, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs) and requires us to disclose competitive terms and match them for Vendor's benefit. That is the wrong direction under the MFN rule and approaches the walk-away position. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere in the document, so the minimal edit to reach the preferred position is deletion of § 7.2; a narrow MFN (one defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Delete § 7.2 reverse MFN / obligation on Customer to disclose and match third-party offers
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 7.2 because it runs the wrong way: it obliges us to disclose and match better third-party offers for Vendor's benefit, which our playbook does not accept (MFN pricing in our favour is welcome). It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer or exclusivity commitment. If Vendor needs something here, we could consider an MFN limited to a single defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
